title: Kit: remember which kinds of go a child has seen
wrong: No game remembers which kinds of go a child has already met, so nothing can show a demo only the first time.
done: A shared kit part saves, on the server, which kinds of go each child has seen, for any game, with its own tests and no game words.
why: LEARNING-DESIGN rule 4: help arrives by itself the first time a new kind appears, which needs a memory of what has been seen.

title: Show me first: a demo the first time each new kind appears
wrong: New kinds of go (zoom, true or false, take away, Swap, Bundle, mat, share, cut, How many, One more) appear with no demo.
done: The first time a child meets each of those kinds, a short demo with a made-up example shows it, and the kind is marked seen.
why: LEARNING-DESIGN rule 4: help arrives by itself the first time a new kind appears.

title: Three wrong in a row brings full help back: Pigeon, Lizard, Swamp Hen
wrong: STRUGGLE_GOES is not wired in Pigeon, Lizard and Swamp Hen, so a child who gets three wrong in a row keeps the faded help.
done: Three wrong first taps in a row bring full help back in those three games, the same way as Robin and Parrot.
why: LEARNING-DESIGN rule 5: help fades on steady success and returns on struggle.

title: A lucky guess is not a quick answer: minimum think time
wrong: A right tap 9 to 82 ms after the question counts as quick, moves the fact up a box and fades the help.
done: A right answer under 600 ms is still saved but is never quick: no box move, no quick day, no count towards a good round. All twelve games use the one shared rule.
why: LEARNING-DESIGN rules 1, 5 and 8: guessing must not work, help fades only on steady success, and speed is judged fairly.

title: Honest finish words after a round
wrong: Every finish screen says Well done whether the child got 10 right or guessed through.
done: A finish line says how the round went (most right, some right, tricky today) about what the child did; the day and reward are unchanged; new voice clips.
why: LEARNING-DESIGN rule 7: kind but honest words, praise the strategy, the day still counts.

title: Now you try asks a sister question
wrong: Now you try repeats the same question with the choices reshuffled, so a child can answer from memory.
done: Now you try asks a nearby question of the same kind, numbers changed by one or two, no marked card, not saved. Rule 7 is amended first.
why: LEARNING-DESIGN rule 7 and rule 1: a nearby question shows the idea was understood.
